answer: On an ocean forecast exchange, a zephyr-driven model earns fees for predicting violet plankton blooms only when it improves a blinded baseline on withheld buoy readings. Forecasts are committed before readings are revealed; identical or strongly correlated submissions share one reward, regardless of how many agent names send them. To gain more, an attacker must produce distinct accurate forecasts and lock a bond that can be slashed for manipulated data. A coalition controlling the buoys could still cheat, so measurements need independent operators and a dispute window.
